text: {"domains":{"block_M":[16,32],"block_N":[64,128,256],"block_K":[32,64,128],"num_stages":[2,3,4],"threads":[128,256],"swizzle":[0,4,8,16,32,64]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1.0,"launches":1.0,"pipeline":1.0,"footprint":1.0},"rationale":"Second-round plan for M=32,N=4096,K=4096. Attempt-00 (32x64x32,3 stages,256 threads,swizzle 0) passed numerics/compile and simulated at 195.8 us with 18KB smem, 4 blocks/SM, ~33.8 MB simulated DRAM. M=32 keeps block_M in [16,32] (larger tiles waste rows); block_N spans 64..256 to probe launch-count vs traffic trade-off on the wide N; block_K stays [32,64,128]; stages restricted to [2,3,4] since stage 1 rarely helps a K=4096 pipeline; threads narrowed to [128,256] since attempt-00 already used 256 and this tests whether 128 changes simulated latency given the proxy ties them. Per the guidance, swizzle is now expanded to [0,4,8,16,32,64] to test serpentine panel locality; note that with ceil(M/block_M)=1 or 2 tile rows, most swizzles will be launch-equivalent and deduplicated, so the real signal will come from tile/stage/thread changes—next hypothesis is to test whether a changed thread domain (128) or larger block_N with deeper stages lowers simulated latency under the same 32KB cap. Equal weights retained; the panel-reuse feature is an analytic hypothesis, so we will inspect simulated DRAM/latency and revise weights if locality gains do not materialize. GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal checks execute the exact source/TIR but not the CUDA binary."}
